Hon’ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, Senior Advocate assisted

Mr. Puran Singh Bisht, Addl. C.S.C. with Mr. 
Sushil Vasistha, Standing Counsel and Mr. 
Virendra Singh Rawat, Brief Holder for the State. 
Heard. 
As prayed, six weeks’ time is granted to 
learned Government pleader to file counter 
affidavit. 
List thereafter. 
No ground to grant interim relief to the 
petitioner is made out at this stage. Interim relief 
application (CLMA 8664 of 2020) is, therefore, 
dismissed. 
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)

Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, learned Senior 
Counsel appearing for the petitioner. 
Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned Additional C.S.C.
for the State of Uttarakhand.
Learned State Counsel has relied upon a 
judgment rendered by Full Bench of this 
Court in WPSS No. 1214 of 2021 in support 
of his contention that claim for 
compassionate appointment by a married 
daughter cannot be reopened after its 
rejection. 
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, learned Senior 
Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits 
that petitioner’s claim was not rejected by 
this Court, therefore, ratio of the said 
judgment will not apply in the present case. 
List this case on 05.04.2023.
In the meantime, learned State Counsel 
shall get instructions in the matter. 
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
28.03.2023

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS 1243/2020
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, Senior
Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional CSC, 
for the State. 
(2) Petitioner’s mother, who was 
employed as a Group ‘D’ employee in 
Collectorate, Pithoragarh, passed away 
on 1.9.2000. After attaining majority, 
petitioner applied for compassionate 
appointment and by that time, she was 
also married. Her application for 
compassionate appointment has been 
rejected by District Magistrate, 
Pithoragarh vide order dated 22.3.2018. 
Feeling aggrieved by rejection of her 
claim, petitioner has approached this 
Court. 
(3) Perusal of the impugned order 
reveals that petitioner’s application has 
been rejected mainly on the ground that 
married daughter does not come within 
the meaning of the term ‘family’, as 
defined under the Dying in Harness 
Rules. Another ground, which has been 
taken, is of delay and laches and it is 
observed that petitioner moved 
application after 11 years of her mother’s 
death. 
(4) Learned State Counsel 
contended that compassionate  appointment cannot be claimed as a 
matter of right and such appointment is 
given to the bereaved family in order to 
tide over the sudden financial crisis 
caused due to death of sole breadwinner
of the family. He further contends that 
petitioner’s mother died on 1.9.2000 and 
petitioner attained majority in the year 
2006, but she applied only in the year 
2011, which indicates that petitioner was 
not under any financial distress. He 
further points out that petitioner has a 
sister, namely, Ms. Kamla Devi and it is 
not known whether she has given NOC to 
petitioner for compassionate 
appointment.
(5) Learned Senior Counsel for the 
petitioner has drawn attention to a Full 
Bench judgment of this Court, rendered 
in Special Appeal No. 187 of 2017, in 
which it has been held that denial of 
opportunity of being considered for 
compassionate appointment to a married 
daughter is violative of Articles 14, 15 
and 16 of the Constitution. Learned 
Senior Counsel for the petitioner thus 
submits that rejection of petitioner’s 
application is contrary to the law laid 
down by the Full Bench of this Court, as 
petitioner’s claim has been rejected 
mainly on the ground that petitioner is a 
married daughter. 
(6) Learned Senior Counsel for the 
petitioner has drawn attention to another 
Full Bench judgment of this Court 
rendered in Writ Petition No. 1214 of 
2021 (S/S). Para 7 and 8 of the said 
judgment are extracted below: “7. Thus, in answering the questions, 
set forth by the learned Single Judge, this Court is 
of the opinion that since there is no mention in the 
conclusion given by the Full Bench of this Court 
that such law declared by this Court will be 
applicable only prospectively not retrospectively it 
has to be taken a declaration of law applicable to all 
cases retrospectively. However, in this case we 
take note of the fact that the petitioner has already 
approached this Court twice. Once, before the 
pronouncement of the Full Bench judgment in 
WPSB No. 391 of 2013, Which has already been 
decided against her. Thus, the judgment declaring 
the law of the Full Bench will not reopen settled 
cases. It can be applied to only case which are 
pending before this Court or which will be filed in 
the future date. By virtue of the judgment passed 
by the Full Bench of this Court referred to above, a 
right which has already been denied and the court 
has not interfered with the same, then the same 
cannot be re-agitated in view of the fact that the 
law has been restated by the Full Bench in the later 
judgment. 
8. As far as applicability of time limit 
provided in Rule 5, Sub-rule (1) clause (iii) of Rules 
1974 that the application for employment is within 
five years from the death of the Government 
servant, we are of the opinion that such five years 
shall be counted in the case of a married daughter, 
who has applied for rehabilitation assistance under 
the Dying in Harness Rules 1974, as applicable to 
the State of Uttarakhand after amendments in the 
Rules 2004, 2010 and 2017, shall be calculated 
from the date of judgment of Full Bench. We take 
this view because of the fact that before the 
judgment pronounced by the Full Bench of this 
Court on 25.03.2019 in SPA No. 187 of 2017, a 
married daughter had no opportunity of filing an 
application for rehabilitation assistance. Hence, the 
matter is answered in the following terms:-
(i) The judgment passed by the Full 
Bench of this Court will have a retrospective effect 
in the sense that it may be applicable to any case 
where death took place after passing of the Rule 
but before judgment is pronounced. 
(ii) The time period will be calculated 
from the date of such judgment as far as  dependent married daughter of an employee dying 
in harness applies. In other words, if any person 
whose father has died prior to the judgment, she 
can make an application for rehabilitation 
assistance within five years from the date of 
passing of the judgment in SPA No. 187 of 2017.”
(7) This Court finds substance in 
the contention raised on behalf of 
petitioner. Since the Full Bench of this 
Court has held that married daughter has 
also right to be considered for 
compassionate appointment, therefore, 
the view taken by District Magistrate is 
contrary and cannot be sustained. 
(8) Accordingly, impugned order 
dated 22.3.2018 is quashed and set 
aside. Matter is remitted back to District 
Magistrate, Pithoragarh to decide
petitioner’s application afresh. 
(9) It is made clear that this Court 
has not expressed any opinion on the 
merits of the case and decision on 
petitioner’s application shall be taken 
strictly in accordance with law. 
(10) With the direction/observation 
as above, this writ petition stands 
disposed of.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 19.4.2023
Pr
